- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict spikes; increase forecast for next 3–5 days by 10–20%.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts downward moves; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp spike in true outcome, model often overshoots in the following 3–7 days; apply a 15–30% downward correction to forecasted values.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >2.0σ above recent 18d mean, reduce by 15–25% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; add 5–10% to forecast for next 3–7 days to catch momentum.
- For horizon >14 days, model underestimates volatility; multiply forecast by 1.15–1.20 if sentiment is volatile or recent price range >1.5x average.
